topics.h: Can your hands dance? Let us say a rhyme and move them!
p: A rhyme is a short poem with a fun beat.
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words.
Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
We say a rhyme slowly and clearly, with a happy voice.

ex.q: Read the rhyme: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap. Tap your knees, tap, tap, tap. Up they go and down they go. Wave to friends and say hello!" Which word rhymes with clap?
st: Say clap. It ends with the sound -ap.
Say tap. It also ends with -ap.
So clap and tap rhyme.

topics.rl: We say action rhymes in the school assembly and at home with Nani and Dadi.

rv.summary: An action rhyme is a short, fun poem. We do the actions as we say it. Rhyming words end with the same sound, like clap and tap.
focus: Read a line and find the action in it
Find words that rhyme by their ending sound
Say a rhyme slowly and clearly
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound: clap, tap, map; go, no
In an action rhyme, we do the actions as we say the words
traps: Don't look at the first letter to find a rhyme. Look at the ending sound.
Top does not rhyme with tap. Map does.

topics.h: Your body is like a busy team. Each part has a job!
p: We see with our eyes and hear with our ears.
We smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
We hold things with our hands and walk with our legs.
We have one nose, two eyes, two ears and two hands.

ex.q: Think it through: I want to smell a rose. Which body part do I use?
st: Smelling is the job of the nose.
Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells.
So I use my nose.

topics.rl: When we wash up in the morning, we clean our face, eyes, ears, hands and feet.

rv.summary: Each body part has a job. We see with our eyes, hear with our ears, smell with our nose and taste with our tongue.
focus: Match each body part to its job
Know how many of each part we have
Spell body words like hand and nose
remember: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes
Hands hold things, legs walk
One nose, two eyes, two ears, two hands
traps: Don't think we have two of every part. We have only one nose.
Don't mix up seeing (eyes) with hearing (ears).

topics.h: Jump! Run! Clap! These words make you move!
p: Some words tell us what we do. They are action words, or doing words.
Run, jump, clap, eat, sleep and write are action words.
We write with our hands. We kick with our feet.
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.

ex.q: Think it through: In "Ravi kicks the ball", which is the action word?
st: Ask: what does Ravi do?
Ravi kicks.
So kicks is the action word.

topics.rl: In PT class, the teacher says: run, jump, stop! These are action words.

rv.summary: Action words, or doing words, tell us what we do, like run, jump, clap, eat and write.
focus: Pick the action word in a sentence
Tell action words apart from naming words
Match an action to the body part that does it
remember: Action words: run, jump, clap, eat, sleep, write
An action word fits after I: I run. I clap.
Ask 'What does he or she do?' to find the action word
traps: Don't pick a naming word like hand or chair as the action word.
Don't match the wrong body part: we write with hands, kick with feet.

topics.t: Polite words: good morning, thank you
topics.h: Magic words make everyone smile. Do you know them?
p: We say good morning when we meet someone in the morning.
We say good afternoon after 12 noon and good evening in the evening.
We say good night when we go to bed.
Please, thank you and sorry are magic words.
We say thank you when someone helps us or gives us something.

ex.q: Think it through: Dadi gives Tara a glass of milk. What should Tara say?
st: Dadi gave Tara something.
When someone gives us something, we say thank you.
So Tara says, "Thank you, Dadi!"

topics.rl: At school we say "Good morning, ma'am" to our teacher. At home we say "Please" when we ask for more dal.

rv.summary: We greet people by the time of day: good morning, good afternoon, good evening and good night. Please, thank you and sorry are magic words.
focus: Pick the right greeting for the time of day
Know when to say please, thank you and sorry
Ask for things in a polite way
remember: Morning: good morning. After 12 noon: good afternoon. Evening: good evening. Bed time: good night.
Say thank you when someone helps you or gives you something
Say sorry when you make a mistake or hurt someone
traps: Don't say good morning all day. After 12 noon it is good afternoon.
Good night is for going to bed, not for waking up.
Don't mix up thank you and sorry.

topics.h: Hello! What is your name? Let us talk nicely!
p: When we meet a friend, we can say hello or namaste.
We ask "How are you?" and answer "I am fine, thank you."
We say "My name is ..." to tell our name.
We say bye or goodbye when we leave.
We speak kindly and wait for our turn to talk.

ex.q: Read: Raju: "Hello! What is your name?" Gita: "My name is Gita." Raju: "How are you, Gita?" What should Gita say now?
st: Raju asked how Gita is.
A polite answer to "How are you?" is "I am fine, thank you."
Gita can also ask, "And you?"

topics.rl: When a guest comes home, we say namaste or hello and ask, "How are you?"

rv.summary: We say hello or namaste when we meet, tell our name, ask 'How are you?' and say bye when we leave. We speak kindly and wait for our turn.
focus: Greet family and friends in a kind way
Answer 'How are you?' and 'What is your name?'
Know words for meeting and for leaving
remember: Meeting: hello, namaste. Leaving: bye, goodbye.
'How are you?' - 'I am fine, thank you.'
'What is your name?' - 'My name is ...'
traps: Don't answer 'How are you?' with your name.
Don't say good morning when you leave. Say bye.
Don't talk when someone else is talking. Wait for your turn.

topics.h: Look closely! A picture is full of tiny stories.
p: First look at the whole picture. Then look at each part.
Say what you see: "I can see a cat."
Tell the colour and size: "I can see a big red ball."
Tell how many: "I can see two birds."
Tell where: "The cat is under the tree."

ex.q: Look: 🌳🐒🐒🐒 (three monkeys near a tree). Tell about the picture in one sentence.
st: What do I see? Monkeys and a tree.
How many monkeys? Count: 1, 2, 3.
Put it together in a sentence.
ex.a: I can see three monkeys near a tree.

topics.rl: When Dadu shows us old photos, we tell him who we see and what they are doing.

rv.summary: To tell about a picture, look at the whole picture first, then say what you see, its colour and size, how many and where it is.
focus: Count things in a picture
Tell colour, size and place
Make a sentence that begins 'I can see ...'
remember: Begin with: I can see ...
Tell colour and size: I can see a big red ball.
Tell where: The cat is under the tree.
traps: Don't skip or count twice when you count.
Don't mix up a colour word (red) with a shape word (round).

topics.h: Everything has a name. Even your toothbrush!
p: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing.
Cat, cow, parrot and tiger are names of animals.
Bag, cup, ball and chair are names of things.
We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds: an apple, an egg, an owl.
We use a before other sounds: a cat, a bag, a dog.

ex.q: Think it through: Is it "a egg" or "an egg"?
st: Say egg. It begins with the e sound.
a, e, i, o, u are vowels.
We use an before a vowel sound.

topics.rl: In the kitchen we can name many things: a cup, a plate, a spoon and an onion!

rv.summary: A naming word tells the name of a person, animal, place or thing. We use an before a, e, i, o, u sounds and a before other sounds.
focus: Sort names into animals and things
Choose a or an before a word
Spell naming words like ball
remember: an apple, an egg, an owl (a, e, i, o, u sounds)
a cat, a bag, a dog (other sounds)
Animals: cat, cow, parrot, tiger. Things: bag, cup, ball, chair.
traps: Don't say 'a apple'. Say an apple.
Don't use an before every word. It is a dog.

topics.ch: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys
topics.h: Shh! Story time! Grandparents know the best old stories.
p: The lesson is a funny folk tale about a cap seller and some naughty monkeys.
A folk tale is an old story. People tell it again and again.
The people and animals in a story are its characters.
When we listen, we look at the speaker and stay quiet.
Here is our own story: Raju and the Bell.

ex.q: Listen: "Raju had a shiny red bell. He sat under a neem tree to rest. Mini the monkey took the bell and climbed up the tree. Mini copies everything she sees. Raju had an idea. He clapped his hands. Mini clapped too! The bell fell down, and Raju picked it up." Who are the characters?
st: Who is in the story? Raju is in it.
A monkey named Mini is in it.
So the characters are Raju and Mini.

topics.rl: At bedtime, Nani or Dadi may tell us an old story they heard when they were small.

rv.summary: A folk tale is an old story that people tell again and again. The people and animals in it are its characters. We listen quietly and look at the speaker.
focus: Find who is in a story (the characters)
Read a line and answer what, who and where
Know good listening manners
remember: Folk tale: an old story told again and again
Characters: the people and animals in a story
In Raju and the Bell, the characters are Raju and Mini the monkey
traps: Don't guess. Read the line to find the answer.
Don't mix up the characters: Mini took the bell, not Raju.

topics.ch: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys
topics.h: Monkey see, monkey do! Can you copy a funny face?
p: To copy means to do the same thing as someone else.
In the lesson, the monkeys copy the cap seller.
Clever means quick at thinking of good ideas.
Raju was clever. He knew Mini would copy him.

ex.q: Think it through: Raju clapped. Mini clapped too. Why did the bell fall?
st: Mini was holding the bell.
She copied Raju and clapped her hands.
To clap, she let go of the bell, so it fell.
ex.a: Mini let go of the bell to copy Raju's clap.

topics.rl: When we play "Simon says" or "Follow the leader", we copy the leader.

rv.summary: To copy means to do the same thing as someone else. Raju was clever: he knew Mini would copy him, so he clapped and Mini dropped the bell.
focus: Know the meaning of copy and clever
Tell why things happen in the story
Find opposites and rhyming words
remember: Copy: do the same thing as someone else
Clever: quick at thinking of good ideas
Opposites: up and down, took and gave
traps: Don't pick a word with the same meaning when asked for the opposite: got is not the opposite of took.
Cup does not rhyme with cap. Map does.

topics.ch: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys
topics.h: Stories are like a train. Each part comes in its turn!
p: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
We use first, next, then and last to tell a story in order.
If we mix up the order, the story does not make sense.

ex.q: Put in order: (a) The bell fell down. (b) Mini took the bell. (c) Raju clapped his hands.
st: First, Mini took the bell.
Next, Raju clapped his hands.
Last, the bell fell down.

topics.rl: We get ready in order: first we wake up, then we brush, then we bathe, then we eat.

rv.summary: A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. We use first, next, then and last to tell it in the right order.
focus: Say what happened first and what happened last
Put story events in order
Use first, next, then and last
remember: Order words: first, next, then, last
A story has a beginning, a middle and an end
traps: Don't mix up first and last.
Don't jump ahead. If the order is mixed up, the story does not make sense.

topics.h: Cock-a-doodle-doo! Wake up, the farm is busy!
p: A farm has fields, and animals like cows, goats, hens, ducks and horses.
A cow gives us milk. A hen lays eggs.
A sheep gives us wool to make warm sweaters.
Baby animals have their own names: a calf, a chick, a puppy, a kitten.

ex.q: Think it through: Which farm animal gives us milk for our chai?
st: Milk comes from cows (and from buffaloes and goats too).
Hens give eggs, not milk.
So a cow is a good answer.

topics.rl: Dahi, paneer and ghee are made from milk. Many families in villages keep cows and buffaloes.

rv.summary: A farm has fields and animals like cows, goats, hens, ducks and horses. A cow gives milk, a hen lays eggs and a sheep gives wool.
focus: Know which farm animal gives what
Know the names of baby animals
Tell farm animals apart from wild animals
remember: Cow: milk. Hen: eggs. Sheep: wool.
Baby animals: calf, chick, puppy, kitten
traps: Don't mix up which animal gives what: hens give eggs, not milk.
A shark is not a farm animal. It lives in the sea.

topics.h: Moo! Quack! Baa! Who is talking?
p: Each animal makes its own sound.
A cow moos. A duck quacks. A hen clucks.
A dog barks. A cat mews (meows). A sheep says baa.
A horse neighs. A donkey brays: hee-haw!
A rooster crows: cock-a-doodle-doo!

ex.q: Read the poem: "Hello, hello, the farm is awake! The ducks go quack beside the lake. The cow says moo, the hen says cluck, and off goes Dadu in his truck!" What does the hen say?
st: Find the hen in the poem.
The poem says: the hen says cluck.
So the hen says cluck.

topics.rl: In a village, the rooster crows early in the morning and wakes everyone up!

rv.summary: Each animal makes its own sound. A cow moos, a duck quacks, a hen clucks, a dog barks and a horse neighs.
focus: Match each animal to its sound
Use the sound word in a sentence: a dog barks
Read a line to find who makes which sound
remember: Cow: moo. Duck: quack. Hen: cluck. Sheep: baa.
Dog barks. Cat mews. Horse neighs. Donkey brays.
Rooster crows: cock-a-doodle-doo!
traps: Don't mix up animal sounds: a dog barks, a cow moos.
Read the right part of the line to see who makes the sound.

topics.h: Cat, hat, mat... Words that sound alike are fun!
p: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Cat, hat and mat rhyme. They all end with -at.
Hen, pen and ten rhyme. They all end with -en.
Words that only begin the same do not rhyme. Cat and cow do not rhyme.
Poems often use rhyming words at the end of lines.

ex.q: Read: "The cow says moo, the hen says cluck, and off goes Dadu in his truck!" Which word rhymes with cluck?
st: Cluck ends with the sound -uck.
Truck also ends with -uck.
So cluck and truck rhyme.

topics.rl: Many songs and rhymes we sing at school have rhyming words, like star and are.

rv.summary: Rhyming words end with the same sound, like cat, hat and mat. Words that only begin the same, like cat and cow, do not rhyme.
focus: Find a word that rhymes by its ending sound
Spot the word that does not rhyme
Find rhyming words in a poem
remember: Rhyming words end with the same sound
-at: cat, hat, mat. -en: hen, pen, ten.
Poems often have rhyming words at the end of lines
traps: Don't pick a word just because it starts the same. Cat and cow do not rhyme.
Pin does not rhyme with pen. Check the ending sound.

topics.h: A picture can tell a story without any words!
p: To read a picture, we ask: Who? What? Where?
Who is in the picture? A girl, a dog, a bird...
What are they doing? Running, eating, flying...
Where are they? In a park, at home, near a river...
We can count the things we see.

ex.q: Look: 👧⚽🌳 (a girl kicks a ball in a park). Who is it? What is she doing? Where is she?
st: Who? A girl.
What is she doing? She is kicking a ball.
Where? In a park, near a tree.
ex.a: A girl is kicking a ball in a park.

topics.rl: Signs on the road and in the bus use pictures, like a picture of a person walking.

rv.summary: To read a picture, we ask Who? What? Where? We can also count the things we see.
focus: Answer who, what and where about a picture
Count the things in a picture
Use picture clues to tell what someone is doing
remember: Who? tells the person or animal
What? tells what they are doing
Where? tells the place
traps: Don't mix up question words: where asks about a place, not a person.
Don't skip or count twice when counting.

topics.h: Red, blue, green! Round, square, three corners! Let us look around!
p: Red, blue, yellow, green, orange, pink, white and black are colours.
Grass is green. Milk is white. A crow is black.
A circle is round, like a roti or a coin.
A triangle has 3 sides. A square has 4 equal sides.
A rectangle has 4 sides, like a door or a book.

ex.q: Think it through: A carrom board has 4 equal sides. What shape is it?
st: Count the sides: 4.
All 4 sides are the same length.
A shape with 4 equal sides and square corners is a square.

topics.rl: Look around: the clock is round, the door is a rectangle, and a slice of watermelon looks like a triangle.

rv.summary: We know colours like red, blue, green and yellow, and shapes: a circle is round, a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 equal sides, and a rectangle has 2 long and 2 short sides.
focus: Name the shape of things we see
Count the sides of a shape
Know colours of things and spell colour words
remember: Circle: round, like a coin or a roti
Triangle: 3 sides. Square: 4 equal sides.
Rectangle: 4 sides, 2 long and 2 short, like a door
Grass is green. Milk is white. A crow is black.
traps: Don't call every 4-sided shape a square. A door is a rectangle.
Yellow has two l's.

topics.h: A trip to the sabzi market! What will we buy?
p: Mango, banana, apple, guava, papaya and grapes are fruits.
Potato, carrot, spinach, onion, brinjal and cauliflower are vegetables.
Many fruits are sweet and we can eat them raw.
We cook many vegetables to make sabzi, dal or soup.
The mango is the national fruit of India.

ex.q: Read: "Pinky goes to the market with Papa. She sees red apples and yellow bananas. Papa buys green spinach and orange carrots. Pinky picks a big mango. "Yum!" she says." Which fruit does Pinky pick?
st: Find Pinky in the story.
The story says: Pinky picks a big mango.
So Pinky picks a mango.

topics.rl: At the market, the fruit seller has mangoes and bananas. The sabzi seller has potatoes and onions.

rv.summary: Mango, banana, apple and guava are fruits. Potato, carrot, spinach and onion are vegetables. The mango is the national fruit of India.
focus: Sort foods into fruits and vegetables
Read a line to find the colour of a food
Spell fruit names like mango
remember: Fruits: mango, banana, apple, guava, papaya, grapes
Vegetables: potato, carrot, spinach, onion, brinjal, cauliflower
The mango is the national fruit of India
traps: Don't mix up fruits and vegetables: spinach is a vegetable.
Match each colour word with the word right after it.

topics.h: Want to run fast and grow strong? Eat well!
p: Fruits, vegetables, dal, rice, roti and milk help us grow.
Drink clean water many times a day.
Wash your hands before you eat.
Chips, sweets and cold drinks are fine only once in a while.
Eat slowly and chew your food well.

ex.q: Think it through: Ravi wants a healthy snack after school. Should he pick a banana or a big packet of chips?
st: A banana is a fruit. Fruits help us stay healthy.
Chips have a lot of salt and oil.
So the banana is the healthier snack.

topics.rl: A good lunch box can have roti, sabzi and a fruit like a guava or an apple.

rv.summary: Fruits, vegetables, dal, rice, roti and milk help us grow. We drink clean water, wash hands before eating and chew food well.
focus: Pick the healthy snack
Know good habits before and while eating
Know which foods to have only once in a while
remember: Wash your hands before you eat
Drink clean water many times a day
Eat slowly and chew your food well
traps: Don't think tasty chips or cold drinks are healthy. Have them only once in a while.
Cold drinks are not as good as water.

topics.h: Do you like karela? Some do, some don't. That is okay!
p: We say "I like ..." for things we enjoy.
We say "I do not like ..." or "I don't like ..." for things we do not enjoy.
We ask "Do you like ...?" to find out.
We answer "Yes, I do." or "No, I don't."

ex.q: Read: Asha: "Do you like idli?" Sam: "Yes, I do. I like idli with sambar." Does Sam like idli?
st: Asha asks a question.
Sam says, "Yes, I do."
So Sam likes idli.

topics.rl: At a birthday party, friends ask each other, "Do you like cake?"

rv.summary: We say 'I like ...' for things we enjoy and 'I don't like ...' for things we do not. We ask 'Do you like ...?' and answer 'Yes, I do.' or 'No, I don't.'
focus: Tell what someone likes and does not like
Answer 'Do you like ...?' the right way
Use I like, not I likes
remember: I like ... / I do not like ... / I don't like ...
Do you like ...? - Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Don't is the short form of do not
traps: Don't miss the word don't. It changes the meaning.
Don't say 'Yes, I am.' Say 'Yes, I do.'
Don't say 'I likes'. Say 'I like'.

topics.h: Hot, wet, cold or full of flowers? Every season is different!
p: Summer is hot. The sun shines bright.
The rainy season brings dark clouds and lots of rain.
After the rains, autumn comes. Then comes winter, which is cold.
Spring comes after winter. Many plants have new leaves and flowers.
The seasons come again and again, every year.

ex.q: Read the poem: "Summer sun is hot and bright. Rainy clouds bring rain at night. Winter mornings, cold and grey. Spring brings flowers, hip hooray!" Which season brings flowers?
st: Find the word flowers in the poem.
The line is: Spring brings flowers.
So spring brings flowers.

topics.rl: We eat cool mangoes in summer, jump in puddles in the rainy season and drink hot soup in winter.

rv.summary: Summer is hot, the rainy season brings rain, autumn comes after the rains, winter is cold, and spring brings new leaves and flowers. The seasons come again every year.
focus: Know what each season is like
Know which season comes after winter
Read a line of a poem and find rhyming words
remember: Summer: hot. Rainy season: rain. Winter: cold. Spring: flowers.
Spring comes after winter
Hot and cold are opposites
traps: Don't mix up summer (hot) and winter (cold).
Warm is not the opposite of hot. Cold is.

topics.h: Would you wear a sweater on a hot day? No way!
p: Weather words: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot and cold.
On hot days we wear light cotton clothes and a cap.
On rainy days we use a raincoat and an umbrella.
On cold days we wear a woollen sweater, a cap and socks.
We dress to keep our body comfortable.

ex.q: Think it through: It is raining hard. Tara has to go to school. What should she take?
st: Rain will make her wet.
A raincoat or an umbrella keeps us dry.
So Tara should take an umbrella or wear a raincoat.

topics.rl: In Delhi winters, children wear sweaters to school. In Chennai summers, they wear light cotton clothes.

rv.summary: Weather can be sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot or cold. We wear cotton on hot days, a raincoat or umbrella on rainy days and woollens on cold days.
focus: Pick the right clothes for the weather
Use clue words to name the weather
Spell weather words like rain
remember: Hot day: light cotton clothes and a cap
Rainy day: raincoat and umbrella
Cold day: woollen sweater, cap and socks
traps: Don't mix up clothes for hot and cold days.
Don't miss the clue word: wind means windy, dark clouds mean cloudy.

topics.h: Sun plus rain can paint the sky! Have you seen a rainbow?
p: A rainbow has seven colours.
The colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
We can remember them as VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.
We can see a rainbow when the sun shines while it rains, or just after rain.
Never look straight at the sun. It can hurt your eyes.

ex.q: Read: "It was a grey, rainy day. Pari looked out of the window. The sun came out and the rain was still falling. A rainbow! Pari took her crayons and drew it with all seven colours." How many colours did Pari use?
st: Find the part about Pari's drawing.
It says she drew it with all seven colours.
A rainbow has seven colours.

topics.rl: We can see rainbow colours in the spray of a garden pipe on a sunny day, and in soap bubbles too.

rv.summary: A rainbow has seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red (VIBGYOR). We can see one when the sun shines while it rains.
focus: Know the seven rainbow colours
Say what each letter of VIBGYOR stands for
Know when we can see a rainbow
remember: A rainbow has 7 colours
VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
Never look straight at the sun
traps: Don't think every colour is in the rainbow. Brown and black are not.
G in VIBGYOR is green, not grey.

topics.h: Close your eyes. Can you see a purple elephant? That is imagination!
p: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
We can draw what we imagine: a flying fish or a pink tiger!
Colour words tell about things: a red kite, a blue sky.
We can tell about our drawing: "This is my house. It has a red door."
Every drawing is special. There is no wrong way to imagine.

ex.q: Think it through: Pari wants to draw a rainbow. What should she do first, and what last?
st: First, she takes paper and crayons.
Next, she draws the curved lines and colours each one.
Last, she shows her drawing to her friends.
ex.a: First get paper and crayons; last show the drawing.

topics.rl: On Children's Day or in art class, we draw and colour pictures and put them on the wall.

rv.summary: To imagine means to make a picture in your mind. We can draw what we imagine, use colour words, and tell about our drawing.
focus: Know the meaning of imagine
Find the colour word in a sentence
Tell about a drawing in a correct sentence
remember: Imagine: make a picture in your mind
Tell about a drawing: This is my house. It has a red door.
There is no wrong way to imagine
traps: Don't mix up colour words (yellow) and size words (big).
Don't put words in the wrong order: say 'This is my red kite.'

qa.q: Read: "Clap your hands, clap, clap, clap." What do the hands do?
qa.e: The line says the hands go clap, clap, clap.

qa.q: Read: "Wave to friends and say hello!" What do we say to friends?
qa.e: The line says: say hello.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with tap?
qa.e: Tap and map both end with the sound -ap.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with go?
qa.e: Go and no both end with the sound -o.

qa.q: Read: "Up they go and down they go." Which word is the opposite of up?
qa.e: Up and down are opposites.

qa.q: How many hands do we clap together?
qa.e: We clap two hands together. One hand cannot clap on its own.

qa.q: Which body part do we use to see a kite?
qa.e: We see things with our eyes.

qa.q: Meena hears a bird sing. Which part helps her hear?
qa.e: We hear sounds with our ears.

qa.q: How many noses do you have?
qa.e: We have just one nose, in the middle of the face.

qa.q: 🖐️ Which is the right spelling for this body part?
qa.e: We spell it h-a-n-d: hand.

qa.q: Nose begins with the letter ___.
qa.e: Nose begins with the sound n, so the letter is n.

qa.q: Which body part tastes a sweet laddoo?
qa.e: We taste food with our tongue.

qa.q: Which is an action word?
qa.e: Jump tells us what we do. Hand is a body part. Red is a colour.

qa.q: Read: "Asha claps her hands." Which word is the action word?
qa.e: Claps tells what Asha does.

qa.q: What do we do with a pencil?
qa.e: We hold a pencil and write with it.

qa.q: I ___ my teeth every morning.
qa.e: We brush our teeth every morning.

qa.q: Which action do we do with our legs?
qa.e: We run with our legs. We eat with our mouth and hear with our ears.

qa.q: Which is NOT an action word?
qa.e: Chair is the name of a thing. Sing and hop are things we do.

qa.q: Ria meets her teacher at 8 in the morning. What should she say?
qa.e: In the morning, we say good morning.

qa.q: Amit is going to bed. What does he say to Mummy?
qa.e: We say good night when we go to bed.

qa.q: Your friend gives you a pencil. What do you say?
qa.e: When someone gives us something, we say thank you.

qa.q: Kabir steps on Neha's foot by mistake. What should he say?
qa.e: We say sorry when we make a mistake or hurt someone.

qa.q: Which is the polite way to ask?
qa.a: May I have a laddoo, please?
qa.e: Using please and may I is polite.

qa.q: It is 2 o'clock in the afternoon. You meet Nani. What do you say?
qa.e: After 12 noon and before evening, we say good afternoon.

qa.q: Read: "Hello! My name is Zoya." What is the girl's name?
qa.e: She says, "My name is Zoya."

qa.q: Your friend asks, "How are you?" What is a good answer?
qa.e: "I am fine, thank you" answers "How are you?"

qa.q: You are leaving your friend's house. What do you say?
qa.e: When we leave, we say bye or goodbye.

qa.q: Which question asks for a name?
qa.e: "What is your name?" asks for a name.

qa.q: Papa is talking on the phone. What should you do?
qa.e: It is polite to wait for our turn to speak.

qa.q: Which is a kind way to greet Dadi?
qa.e: Namaste and "How are you?" are kind and polite.

qa.q: Look: 🐄🐄. How many cows can you see?
qa.e: Count the cows: 1, 2. There are two cows.

qa.q: Look: 🐦🐦🐦🐦 on a wire. How many birds?
qa.e: Count: 1, 2, 3, 4. There are four birds.

qa.q: Look: 🐘 and 🐭. Which one is big?
qa.e: An elephant is big. A mouse is small.

qa.q: Which sentence tells about 🌳🐱 (a cat under a tree)?
qa.a: The cat is under the tree.
qa.e: The cat sits under the tree, so we say "under the tree".

qa.q: Look: 🎈 (a red balloon). Which word tells its colour?
qa.e: Red is a colour word.

qa.q: What is a good way to start telling about a picture?
qa.e: "I can see" tells what is in the picture.

qa.q: Which is the name of an animal?
qa.e: A tiger is an animal. A table and a pencil are things.

qa.q: Which is the name of a thing?
qa.e: We eat with a spoon. It is a thing, not an animal.

qa.q: 🍎 Choose the right words for this picture.
qa.e: Apple begins with the a sound, a vowel. So we say an apple.

qa.q: 🐕 Which words name this pet the right way?
qa.e: Dog begins with d, not a vowel. So we say a dog.

qa.q: Read: "The parrot sits on a branch." Which word names a bird?
qa.e: Parrot is the name of a bird.

qa.q: ⚽ Which is the right spelling for this toy?
qa.e: We spell it b-a-l-l: ball.

qa.q: Read: "Raju had a shiny red bell." What colour was the bell?
qa.e: The line says the bell was shiny and red.

qa.q: Read: "He sat under a neem tree to rest." Where did Raju sit?
qa.e: The line says he sat under a neem tree.

qa.q: Read: "Mini the monkey took the bell." Who took the bell?
qa.e: The line says Mini the monkey took it.

qa.q: What is a folk tale?
qa.a: An old story told again and again
qa.e: Folk tales are old stories passed on by people.

qa.q: How should we listen to a story?
qa.e: Good listeners stay quiet and look at the speaker.

qa.q: Read: "Mini climbed up the tree." Climbed up means Mini went ___.
qa.e: Climbing up means going higher.

qa.q: Raju waves. Mini waves too. What is Mini doing?
qa.e: Doing the same as someone else is copying.

qa.q: Which word means quick at thinking of good ideas?
qa.e: A clever person thinks of good ideas quickly.

qa.q: Raju knew Mini copies everything. Then he clapped. Why did he clap?
qa.a: He knew Mini would copy him
qa.e: Raju wanted Mini to copy him and drop the bell.

qa.q: Which is the opposite of up?
qa.e: Up and down are opposites.

qa.q: Read: "Mini took the bell." The opposite of took is ___.
qa.e: Take and give are opposites. Took and gave are opposites too.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with cap?
qa.e: Cap and map both end with the sound -ap.

qa.q: Story: Raju sat under a tree. Mini took the bell. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened first?
qa.e: The story begins with Raju resting under a tree.

qa.q: Story: Mini took the bell. Raju clapped. The bell fell. Raju picked it up. What happened last?
qa.e: At the end, the bell fell and Raju picked it up.

qa.q: Raju clapped. Mini copies everything she sees. What did Mini do next?
qa.e: Mini copied Raju and clapped.

qa.q: Which word tells the end of a list of steps?
qa.e: Last comes at the end.

qa.q: First I wake up. Next I brush my teeth. Then I ___.
qa.e: After waking and brushing, we eat breakfast.

qa.q: Which comes first in a story?
qa.e: A story starts with the beginning.

qa.q: Which animal lays eggs?
qa.e: A hen lays eggs.

qa.q: What do we get from sheep?
qa.e: Sheep give wool. It is used to make sweaters.

qa.q: A baby dog is called a ___.
qa.e: A baby dog is a puppy.

qa.q: Read: "The ducks go quack beside the lake." Where are the ducks?
qa.e: The line says the ducks are beside the lake.

qa.q: Read: "Off goes Dadu in his truck!" How does Dadu go?
qa.e: The line says Dadu goes in his truck.

qa.q: Which one is a farm animal?
qa.e: Goats live on farms. Sharks live in the sea and penguins live in very cold places.

qa.q: What sound does a duck make?
qa.e: Ducks say quack.

qa.q: Which animal says moo?
qa.e: A cow says moo.

qa.q: A dog ___.
qa.e: We say a dog barks.

qa.q: Which animal says cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning?
qa.e: A rooster crows cock-a-doodle-doo.

qa.q: A horse ___.
qa.e: We say a horse neighs.

qa.q: Read: "The cow says moo, the hen says cluck." Who says cluck?
qa.e: The line says the hen says cluck.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with hen?
qa.e: Hen and ten both end with -en.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with cat?
qa.e: Cat and mat both end with -at.

qa.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
qa.e: Dog and log both end with -og.

qa.q: Read: "The farm is awake! The ducks go quack beside the lake." Which word rhymes with awake?
qa.e: Awake and lake both end with the sound -ake.

qa.q: Which word does NOT rhyme with pen?
qa.e: Pin ends with -in. Pen, ten and hen end with -en.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with goat?
qa.e: Goat and coat both end with -oat.

qa.q: Look: 🐱🐱🐱 on a wall. How many cats?
qa.e: Count: 1, 2, 3. There are three cats.

qa.q: Look: 🦋🦋🦋🦋🦋 near flowers. How many butterflies?
qa.e: Count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are five butterflies.

qa.q: Look: 👦📖 (a boy with a book). What is the boy doing?
qa.e: A boy with an open book is reading.

qa.q: Look: 🐠 in a pond. Where is the fish?
qa.e: The fish is in the pond.

qa.q: Which question asks about a place?
qa.e: Where asks about the place.

qa.q: Look: 👩‍🍳🍲 (Amma at the stove). Which word tells what she is doing?
qa.e: Amma is at the stove with a pot, so she is cooking.

qa.q: What shape is a coin?
qa.e: A coin is round, so it is a circle.

qa.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
qa.e: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

qa.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides?
qa.e: A square has 4 sides, all the same length.

qa.q: A door has 4 sides. Two are long and two are short. What shape is it?
qa.e: A shape with 2 long and 2 short sides is a rectangle.

qa.q: What colour is grass?
qa.e: Grass is green.

qa.q: Which is the right spelling for the colour of a ripe banana?
qa.e: We spell it y-e-l-l-o-w, with two l's.

qa.q: Which one is a fruit?
qa.e: A banana is a fruit. Potato and onion are vegetables.

qa.q: Which one is a vegetable?
qa.e: Spinach (palak) is a leafy vegetable.

qa.q: Which is the national fruit of India?
qa.e: The mango is the national fruit of India.

qa.q: Read: "Papa buys green spinach and orange carrots." What colour are the carrots?
qa.e: The line says orange carrots. Green tells about the spinach.

qa.q: Read: "She sees red apples and yellow bananas." What colour are the bananas?
qa.e: The line says yellow bananas.

qa.q: 🥭 Which is the right spelling for this fruit?
qa.e: We spell it m-a-n-g-o: mango.

qa.q: What should we do before eating?
qa.e: Clean hands keep germs away from our food.

qa.q: Which is a healthy snack?
qa.e: An apple is a fruit. It is a healthy snack.

qa.q: What should we drink many times a day?
qa.e: Our body needs clean water every day.

qa.q: Read: "Meena eats roti, dal and a guava for lunch." Which fruit does Meena eat?
qa.e: Guava is the fruit. Roti and dal are not fruits.

qa.q: How should we eat our food?
qa.e: Chewing food well helps our body use it.

qa.q: Healthy food helps us ___.
qa.e: Healthy food helps our body grow strong.

qa.q: Read: "I like grapes. I don't like onions." What does the child like?
qa.e: The child says, "I like grapes."

qa.q: Read: "I like grapes. I don't like onions." What does the child not like?
qa.e: "I don't like onions" means the child does not enjoy onions.

qa.q: Your friend asks, "Do you like milk?" You do. What do you say?
qa.e: To answer "Do you like...?" with yes, we say "Yes, I do."

qa.q: Which sentence is correct?
qa.e: With I, we say like: I like dosa.

qa.q: Which word means the same as "do not"?
qa.e: Don't is the short form of do not.

qa.q: Riya does not like karela. What is kind to say?
qa.a: That is okay. I like it.
qa.e: People can like different foods. We speak kindly about it.

qa.q: Read: "Summer sun is hot and bright." What is the summer sun like?
qa.e: The line says the summer sun is hot and bright.

qa.q: Read: "Winter mornings, cold and grey." Which season has cold mornings?
qa.e: The line says winter mornings are cold.

qa.q: Read: "Rainy clouds bring rain at night." What do the clouds bring?
qa.e: The line says rainy clouds bring rain.

qa.q: Read: "Summer sun is hot and bright." Which word rhymes with bright?
qa.e: Bright and night both end with the sound -ight.

qa.q: Which season comes after winter?
qa.e: After winter comes spring.

qa.q: Which is the opposite of hot?
qa.e: Hot and cold are opposites.

qa.q: It is a cold winter morning. What should Rohan wear?
qa.e: Woollen clothes keep us warm when it is cold.

qa.q: It is a very hot summer day. What is best to wear?
qa.e: Cotton clothes are light and cool for hot days.

qa.q: What do we use to stay dry in the rain?
qa.e: An umbrella keeps the rain off us.

qa.q: Read: "The wind blows the kites high in the sky." What is the weather like?
qa.e: Wind blowing hard means it is windy.

qa.q: 🌧️ Which is the right spelling for water falling from clouds?
qa.e: We spell it r-a-i-n: rain.

qa.q: The sky is full of dark clouds. Which word fits?
qa.e: When clouds cover the sky, it is cloudy.

qa.q: How many colours are in a rainbow?
qa.e: A rainbow has seven colours: VIBGYOR.

qa.q: Which colour is in the rainbow?
qa.e: Indigo is the I in VIBGYOR. Brown and black are not rainbow colours.

qa.q: In VIBGYOR, what does G stand for?
qa.e: G stands for green.

qa.q: Read: "The sun came out and the rain was still falling." What may Pari see in the sky now?
qa.e: Sun and rain together can make a rainbow.

qa.q: Read: "It was a grey, rainy day." What was the day like?
qa.e: The line says it was a grey, rainy day.

qa.q: 🍊 Which is the right spelling for this colour?
qa.e: We spell it o-r-a-n-g-e: orange.

qa.q: What does imagine mean?
qa.a: To make a picture in your mind
qa.e: When we imagine, we see a picture in our mind.

qa.q: Read: "Pari drew a big yellow sun." Which word tells the colour?
qa.e: Yellow is the colour word. Big tells size.

qa.q: Read: "Pari drew a big yellow sun." Who drew the sun?
qa.e: The line says Pari drew it.

qa.q: What do we use to colour a picture?
qa.e: We colour with crayons or colour pencils.

qa.q: Which sentence tells about a drawing?
qa.e: "This is my red kite" is a correct sentence about a drawing.

qa.q: Blue paint and yellow paint mixed together make ___.
qa.e: Blue and yellow paint mix to make green.
